Open Start and type your farm name and your own limits in the yellow cells: healthy pH, organic matter target, margin per hectare you want, warning days and the share of rain a crop can use.
Fill Fields Register with each field: area, soil, irrigation and supervisor. Tenure, crop, status and soil checks fill in from the other sheets.
List your crops on Crops and Varieties with cycle, yield, price, seed rate, water need and the rest years between two crops.
Price each crop for one hectare on Crop Budget. The margin, break-even yield and break-even price fill in.
Build the year on Season Plan: one row for each field and season with crop, sowing date, harvest date and area. Use Next season for the plan after this one.
Enter the last five seasons of every field on Rotation History, then read Rotation Check for same crop, same family and rest year warnings.
Type the yield you want for each field on Yield Targets and adjust yield, price and extra costs on Gross Margin Forecast.
Plan seed on Seed Plan and soil work on Soil Improvement. Record every soil test on Soil Tests.
Enter owned and leased land on Land Tenure and Rent, boundaries on Field Access, and field problems on Field Problems.
Use Planting Windows, Water Need, Cover Crops, Variety Trials, Land Use Balance and Crop Calendar to plan the year month by month.

Use the 13 calculators for seed, plant population, sowing date, margin, break-even, rotation fit, crop ranking, lime, rent per tonne, area, yield estimate, planting window and price and yield what-if.
Print 9 sheets and 9 letters, follow 9 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Crop Planning Dashboard and Charts every week: sowing, seed orders, rotation, soil checks, margin and production.
Run daily field work, spraying and harvest records with built-in checks
Daily field work, spray records, intervals, loads and yield per field
Pre-harvest interval tracker for every field
the latest spray, every label interval and the re-entry time give the earliest harvest date and a warning when the planned harvest clashes with it
Spray records with record and wind checks
product, dose, area, water and wind are checked, and a missing product or dose or a spray in too much wind is flagged at once
every scouting report is compared with the threshold of that pest on that crop and shows how many times over it is and the product to use
Growing degree days and harvest forecast
degree days from your weather log show the progress of each crop and the forecast harvest date against the planned date
Weather log with workable day check
each day is marked workable, wet, storm or frost from your own limits, with rain, rain days and days lost totalled for the month
each weighed load shows tonnes, the weight lost when drying to safe moisture and a check of too wet, needs drying or dry enough
Yield per field against the target
tonnes from the load log divided by the area give yield per hectare, the gap to target, the value and a verdict once the harvest is done
Work orders against the operations log
hectares and hours logged in the week are set against the plan and each order is marked not started, behind, on schedule or ahead
Operations log with cost per hectare
hours, people, machine rate and fuel give labour, machine and fuel cost, the cost per hectare and the rain on the day of every job
the rate error of each sprayer and drill is checked against your tolerance, and the next date is worked out from the latest record only
hours by kind of work, hours per week over the last four weeks and the labour cost are totalled for each person and compared with the contract
area, share of yield lost and the field target give tonnes and money lost, and each loss shows replanted, replant needed or accept loss

Field operations log: every job in every field
One row for each job with task, field, machine, operator, hours and area; labour, machine and fuel cost, cost per hectare, rain on the day and a work-day check fill in.
Sowing records: seed lot, rate, depth and area
One row for each sowing with seed lot, planned and real rate, depth and row spacing; seed used, rate error, a rate check and the emergence walk fill in.
Spray records: product, dose, area, wind and operator
One row for each spray job with product, dose, area, water, wind and the label intervals; product used, tank loads, wind check, earliest harvest, re-entry date and a record check fill in.
Pre-harvest interval and re-entry tracker for every field
One row for each field; the latest spray, its product, the earliest harvest date from every label interval, days left, re-entry from and a clash with the planned harvest fill in.
Scouting reports: pests, diseases and weeds in each field
One row for each scouting walk with the crop, the pest, the level found and plants checked; the action threshold, the check against it, the product to use and the times over fill in.
Pest and disease action thresholds for every crop
One row for each pest and crop with the level that needs action, the product and the label intervals; reports, reports above it, the highest recent level and a check fill in from scouting.
Weed control log: passes, labour and how well they worked
One row for each weed control pass with method, weeds, area, workers and hours and the weed cover before and after; weeds controlled, a check against your goal, labour hours and cost fill in.
Harvest log: every load with weight and moisture
One row for each load with field, crop, weight, moisture and weigh ticket; tonnes, moisture shrink, tonnes after shrink and a drying check fill in.
Harvest crew and machine hours for every harvest day
One row for each harvest day with machine, operator, hours, crew size, area and fuel; machine, fuel and labour cost, cost per hectare, hectares per hour and litres per hectare fill in.
Yield per field and season against the target
One row for each field and season with the area, the target yield and the price; tonnes from the harvest loads, harvest area, yield, value, gap to target and a verdict fill in.
Daily farm diary: weather, work, people and issues
One row for each day with the weather, people on site, the main work and any issue; jobs and machine hours from the operations log, rain from the weather log and an on-time check fill in.
Weather log: rain, temperature and wind every day
One row for each day with the lowest and highest temperature, rain and wind; degree days, a work-day check and the totals of the month fill in.
Field rain gauge readings against the weather station
One row for each reading from a field gauge; the station rain of the same day, the difference and a check of whether the field was wetter, drier or close fill in.
Frost, hail and storm events and the damage they did
One row for each event with field, area and damage; the crop, share of the field, tonnes and value lost and whether the damage was inspected fill in.
Weekly work orders: what is planned and what was done
One row for each job planned for a week with machine, operator, area and hours; hectares and hours really done from the operations log, the share done and a schedule check fill in.
Operator hours per task, overtime and labour cost
One row for each operator with role, phone, cost per hour and contract hours; hours by kind of work, hours this season, weekly average, overtime check and labour cost fill in from the log.
Crop growth stage of every field with a harvest forecast
One row for each field with crop, stage, start date, planned harvest and degree days needed; degree days so far, progress, forecast harvest date, a schedule check and the harvest so far fill in.
Sprayer and seed drill calibration records
One row for each calibration with the device, the target and the measured rate; the error, a rate check, the next date due and whether the latest check of each device is in date fill in.
One row for each loss with cause, area, share of yield lost and any replanting; tonnes and value lost, the decision to replant or accept the loss and the days since fill in.
Contractor work records: spraying, harvesting and other jobs
One row for each contractor job with service, field, area, rate and phone; cost, whether the work record is signed and the days it stays unsigned fill in.

Supervisor: work order for the field
Hello, today's work order for {field}: {task} with {machine}, {planned_ha} ha in {hours_plan} hours. Operator: {operator}. Please confirm before 7:00.
Hello {supervisor}, we may have a spray window tomorrow on {field} ({crop}, {area_ha} ha). Check the wind at 6:00 and tell me if the team can start.
Hello {supervisor}, the wind is too strong for spraying. Stop the sprayer on {field} ({crop}) and wait until it drops. Tell me when you restart.
Hello {supervisor}, harvest of {crop} on {field} is planned for {harvest_plan} ({area_ha} ha). Please check the machines and the trailers the day before.
Hello {supervisor}, {field} shows {loads_n} loads and {loads_t} t this season, moisture {moist}. Please send the missing weigh tickets today.
Hello {operator}, take {machine} to {field} for {task} (week of {week_start}, {planned_ha} ha). Please check fuel and grease first.
Hello {operator}, the {device} calibration status is: {state}. The next check is due on {next_due}. Please book the test with the manager.
Hello {operator}, after spraying {field} on {date} please rinse the tank and the nozzles with clean water and drain the rinse away from ditches.
Hello {contractor}, we book {service} on {field} for {date}: {area_ha} ha at {rate_ha} per ha. Please confirm your crew and arrival time.
Hello {contractor}, your crew is expected on {field} ({area_ha} ha) on {date}. Please bring your weigh record and call the gate on arrival.
Hello {contractor}, please sign the work record for {field} ({area_ha} ha), done on {date}. Cost {cost}. Status: {state}.
Hello, scouting on {field} ({crop}) found {pest} at {level}, threshold {threshold}. {photos} photos are ready. Please tell me what to do.
Hello, {pest} on {field} is {times} times the threshold ({level} against {threshold}). Product on the plan: {product}. Please confirm the spray.
Hello, the interval on {field} ends on {earliest} after {product}. Planned harvest {plan}. Date check: {clash}. Please confirm.
Hello, spray record {sp_id} on {field} of {date} shows: {state}. Please ask {operator} to complete it today.
Hello, {field} ({crop}, {season}) gave {yield_ha} t/ha against a target of {target_t_ha}, {gap_t} t short. Please send the reasons before Friday.
Hello {recorded_by}, frost is possible tonight, with lows near {tmin} C. Cover tender crops before dark and record the lowest temperature at first light.
Hello, {kind} hit {field} on {date}: {area_ha} ha, damage {damage_pct}. Please inspect the {crop} today and send photos.
Hello, rain stops work. {task} on {field} ({planned_ha} ha, week of {week_start}) moves. Please send me a new plan by noon.
Hello {operator}, the weeding team goes to {field} ({area_ha} ha) using {method}: {workers} people, {hours} hours. Meet at the shed at 6:30.
Hello, {field} needs replanting: {replant_ha} ha of {crop} after {cause}. Decision: {state}. Please prepare seed and the drill.
Hello {recorded_by}, the weather log for {date} must be complete today: rain, lowest and highest temperature and wind. Please enter it.
Hello, we need {litres} litres of {product} for {field} ({crop}). Batch {batch} was used on {date}. Please confirm the delivery date.
Hello, we return unopened {product}, batch {batch}, bought for {field}. Please collect it this week and send a credit note.
Hello, {kind} hit your field {field} on {date}. About {area_ha} ha are damaged ({damage_pct}), an estimated {loss_t} t. We will send the inspection report.
Hello {operator}, please send your timesheet for {date} on {field}: {hours} hours with {machine}, crew of {crew}. Thank you.
Staff: diary entry due by 6 pm
Hello {author}, the diary for {date} shows: {state}. Please enter the weather, the work and the issues by 6 pm every day.
Hello, please check spray {sp_id}: {product} at {dose_l_ha} l/ha on {area_ha} ha of {field}, wind {wind_kmh} km/h. Wind check: {wind_state}.
Hello {name}, you worked {week_avg} hours a week over the last four weeks against {hours_week} in your contract. Please talk to me about time off.
Hello {name}, your hours this month are {h_month} and this season {h_season}. Please check them and tell me about any mistake.
Entry {col:diary.dy_id} for {col:diary.date}. Written by {col:diary.author} on {col:diary.entered_on}. Entry check: {col:diary.state}.
Weather: {col:diary.cond}, with {col:diary.rain} mm of rain recorded. People on site: {col:diary.people}.
Main work: {col:diary.tasks}. The operations log shows {col:diary.ops_n} jobs and {col:diary.ops_h} machine hours for the day.
The diary is written each day by 6 pm. A late entry is marked as late and the days of delay are counted.

Product: {col:sprays.product}, batch {col:sprays.batch}. Dose: {col:sprays.dose_l_ha} litres per hectare on {col:sprays.area_ha} hectares, so {col:sprays.litres} litres of product in {col:sprays.water_l_ha} litres of water per hectare.
Conditions: wind {col:sprays.wind_kmh} km/h, temperature {col:sprays.temp_c} C. Wind check: {col:sprays.wind_state}. Operator: {col:sprays.operator}.

Pre-harvest interval: {col:sprays.phi_days} days, so the earliest harvest is {col:sprays.harvest_ok}. Re-entry: {col:sprays.rei_h} hours, so people may enter again from {col:sprays.reentry}. Record check: {col:sprays.state}.
This record is kept with the product label and the safety data sheet for inspection.

The last spray was on {col:phi.last_spray} with {col:phi.product}. The earliest harvest date over all label intervals is {col:phi.earliest}, which leaves {col:phi.days_left} days to wait. Interval check: {col:phi.state}.
People may enter the field again from {col:phi.entry_from} ({col:phi.rei} hours). Re-entry check: {col:phi.entry}.
The planned harvest date is {col:phi.plan}. Harvest date check: {col:phi.clash}.
Harvest does not start before the earliest date. If the plan clashes with it, the crop manager moves the harvest date and tells the field supervisor.

Finding: {col:scout.pest} on {col:scout.level} of {col:scout.checked} plants checked, with {col:scout.photos} photos taken. The action threshold is {col:scout.threshold}, so the finding is {col:scout.times} times the threshold.
Threshold check: {col:scout.state}. Product to use if action is needed: {col:scout.product}.
The report is {col:scout.age} days old. The crop adviser reads it at {col:scout.adv_phone} before any spray is ordered.
A spray is ordered only when the finding is at or above the threshold and the weather allows spraying.
The crop is at the stage {col:stages.stage}. The harvest was planned for {col:stages.harvest_plan}. Schedule check: {col:stages.state}.

This season {col:stages.loads_n} loads were weighed, {col:stages.loads_t} tonnes in total, at an average moisture of {col:stages.moist}. That is {col:stages.yield_now} tonnes per hectare on the whole field.
The field had {col:stages.ops_n} jobs and {col:stages.sprays_n} sprays this season, and {col:stages.rain_since} mm of rain since the start.
The report is filed with the weigh tickets of the field.

The target was {col:yield.target_t_ha} tonnes per hectare, or {col:yield.target_t} tonnes. {col:yield.loads_n} loads were weighed, {col:yield.tonnes} tonnes in total, from {col:yield.harv_ha} hectares harvested.
The yield is {col:yield.yield_ha} tonnes per hectare, which is {col:yield.vs_target} against the target. Verdict: {col:yield.state}. Tonnes below target: {col:yield.gap_t}.
The harvest is worth {col:yield.value} at {col:yield.price_t} per tonne. The average moisture was {col:yield.moist}.
We use this report to set the targets of the next season.
Month starting {col:weather.month}. Day {col:weather.date} is used as the example below.

On {col:weather.date} the lowest temperature was {col:weather.tmin} C, the highest {col:weather.tmax} C, rain {col:weather.rain_mm} mm and wind {col:weather.wind_kmh} km/h. Work day check: {col:weather.work}.

In the month there were {col:weather.m_rain} mm of rain on {col:weather.m_rain_days} days. The average lowest temperature was {col:weather.m_tmin} C and {col:weather.m_lost} days were lost to weather.
Recorded by {col:weather.recorded_by}. The field limits are in the settings: rain that stops work {set:rain_stop} mm and storm wind {set:storm_wind} km/h.
Name: {col:crew.name}. Role: {col:crew.role}. Phone: {col:crew.phone}. Cost per hour: {col:crew.cost_h}.

Hours this month: {col:crew.h_month}. Land work {col:crew.h_land}, crop care {col:crew.h_care}, irrigation {col:crew.h_irr}, harvest and haulage {col:crew.h_harv}. Hours this season: {col:crew.h_season}.
The average of the last four weeks is {col:crew.week_avg} hours a week against {col:crew.hours_week} contract hours. Overtime check: {col:crew.state}.
